title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Ligand-controlled hydrolysis of lanthanide ions, using high pH and multidentate supporting ligands, assembles hydroxide clusters around a cubane-like [Ln4(μ3-OH)4]8+ motif, and higher-nuclearity products that can be built from those motifs commonly contain small anions that the authors interpret as templates.
explanation: The Account traces the 1999–2006 development of this route and uses it as the basis for later nuclearity (>25) work. The cubane is presented as a recurring building unit rather than a single-compound curiosity.
scope: Lanthanide hydroxide clusters, lanthanide-exclusive or later extended to 3d–4f species.
conditions: High-pH hydrolysis with multidentate ligands; small anions present in nearly all higher-nuclearity clusters that are formally assembled from smaller motifs.
caveats: The Account treats templating as a structural inference from the frequent presence of anions, not as a fully proven mechanism for every cluster.
